deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform is prevented from destroying or abandoning the egress policy. Deletion-blocking flags are security-impacting under the prevent-destructive-loss archetype because accidental removal of an enforced perimeter egress policy can weaken boundary protections, so it is covered by the deletion_policy policy.

perimeter.description: The name of the Service Perimeter to add this resource to.
perimeter.rationale: This argument identifies the Service Perimeter that the egress policy belongs to. It is required for resource placement, but it does not independently define the allowed egress source, destination, identity, service, method, permission, or role.

title.description: Human readable title. Must be unique within the perimeter. Does not affect behavior.
title.rationale: This argument is a human-readable title used for identification. The provider description states that it does not affect behaviour, so it does not directly change the security posture of the enforced egress rule.

egress_from.description: Defines conditions on the source of a request causing this 'EgressPolicy' to apply.

egress_from.identities.description:
Identities can be an individual user, service account, Google group,
or third-party identity. For third-party identity, only single identities
are supported and other identity types are not supported.The v1 identities
that have the prefix user, group and serviceAccount in
https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/principal-identifiers#v1 are supported.
egress_from.identities.rationale: This argument defines the specific identities that can match the egress rule. Allowing unapproved users, groups, service accounts, or external identities can broaden who is able to send traffic outside the perimeter, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_from.identities policy.

egress_from.identity_type.description:
Specifies the type of identities that are allowed access to outside the
perimeter. If left unspecified, then members of 'identities' field will
be allowed access. Possible values: ["ANY_IDENTITY", "ANY_USER_ACCOUNT", "ANY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"]
egress_from.identity_type.rationale: This argument controls the type of identities that can match the egress rule. Broad values such as ANY_IDENTITY can allow a wider set of principals to send traffic outside the perimeter, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_from.identity_type policy.

egress_from.source_restriction.description: Whether to enforce traffic restrictions based on 'sources' field. If the 'sources' field is non-empty, then this field must be set to 'SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED'. Possible values: ["SOURCE_RESTRICTION_UNSPECIFIED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_ENABLED", "SOURCE_RESTRICTION_DISABLED"]
egress_from.source_restriction.rationale: This argument controls whether source restrictions are enforced when source conditions are configured. Because it is an enum with an unspecified/default sentinel and can affect whether egress source controls are applied, it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_from.source_restriction policy.

egress_from.sources.description: Sources that this EgressPolicy authorizes access from.

egress_from.sources.access_level.description: An AccessLevel resource name that allows resources outside the ServicePerimeter to be accessed from the inside.
egress_from.sources.access_level.rationale: This argument references an AccessLevel used as a source condition. The security posture depends on the separately managed AccessLevel definition rather than this reference string alone, so this resource-level policy set does not enforce it directly.

egress_from.sources.resource.description:
A Google Cloud resource that is allowed to egress the perimeter.
Requests from these resources are allowed to access data outside the perimeter.
Currently only projects are allowed. Project format: 'projects/{project_number}'.
The resource may be in any Google Cloud organization, not just the
organization that the perimeter is defined in. '*' is not allowed, the
case of allowing all Google Cloud resources only is not supported.
egress_from.sources.resource.rationale: This argument defines which project resources are allowed as sources for egress traffic. Since it controls source-side exposure across the service perimeter boundary, it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_from.sources.resource policy.

egress_to.description:
Defines the conditions on the 'ApiOperation' and destination resources that
cause this 'EgressPolicy' to apply.

egress_to.external_resources.description:
A list of external resources that are allowed to be accessed. A request
matches if it contains an external resource in this list (Example:
s3://bucket/path). Currently '*' is not allowed.
egress_to.external_resources.rationale: This argument defines external resource URIs that are permitted by the egress policy. Because it controls data exfiltration scope and external access allowlisting, it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_to.external_resources policy.

egress_to.resources.description:
A list of resources, currently only projects in the form
'projects/<projectnumber>', that match this to stanza. A request matches
if it contains a resource in this list. If * is specified for resources,
then this 'EgressTo' rule will authorize access to all resources outside
the perimeter.
egress_to.resources.rationale: This argument defines destination resources outside the perimeter. A wildcard value can authorize access to all resources outside the perimeter, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_to.resources policy.

egress_to.roles.description:
A list of IAM roles that represent the set of operations that the sources
specified in the corresponding 'EgressFrom'
are allowed to perform.
egress_to.roles.rationale: This argument specifies IAM roles for egress operations. Role selection can be team-dependent and may overlap with organisation-specific IAM policy guidance, so this resource-level policy set does not enforce it directly.

egress_to.operations.description:
A list of 'ApiOperations' that this egress rule applies to. A request matches
if it contains an operation/service in this list.

egress_to.operations.service_name.description:
The name of the API whose methods or permissions the 'IngressPolicy' or
'EgressPolicy' want to allow. A single 'ApiOperation' with serviceName
field set to '*' will allow all methods AND permissions for all services.
egress_to.operations.service_name.rationale: This argument defines the Google Cloud service whose methods or permissions are allowed. A wildcard service name can allow all methods and permissions for all services, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_to.operations.service_name policy.

egress_to.operations.method_selectors.description:
API methods or permissions to allow. Method or permission must belong
to the service specified by 'serviceName' field. A single MethodSelector
entry with '*' specified for the 'method' field will allow all methods
AND permissions for the service specified in 'serviceName'.

egress_to.operations.method_selectors.me.description:
Value for 'method' should be a valid method name for the corresponding
'serviceName' in 'ApiOperation'. If '*' used as value for method,
then ALL methods and permissions are allowed.
egress_to.operations.method_selectors.me.rationale: This argument defines the API method allowed for the selected service. A wildcard method can allow all methods and permissions for that service, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_to.operations.method_selectors.method policy.

egress_to.operations.method_selectors.pe.description:
Value for permission should be a valid Cloud IAM permission for the
corresponding 'serviceName' in 'ApiOperation'.
egress_to.operations.method_selectors.pe.rationale: This argument defines the IAM permission allowed for the selected service. Allowing unapproved or write-level permissions can broaden access outside the perimeter, so it is security-impacting and is covered by the egress_to.operations.method_selectors.permission policy.
